groups.name: People & family
groups.intro: Learn every noun together with its article. Gender is mostly arbitrary, so the article is part of the word. der is blue, die is red, das is green.

groups.name: Article (der/die/das)
groups.intro: Type the correct article for each noun.

groups.name: Case forms
groups.intro: Type the definite article in the given case (Akkusativ, Dativ, Genitiv).

groups.name: Plural forms
groups.intro: Type the plural form (with its article).

groups.name: Food & drink
groups.intro: Many nouns ending in -e are feminine (die Suppe, die Lampe). There are exceptions, so keep checking the article.

groups.name: Home & things
groups.intro: Useful endings: -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft and -ion are always feminine. Diminutives in -chen and -lein are always neuter.

groups.name: Time
groups.intro: Time words show up in almost every sentence. Watch the articles: der Tag, die Woche, das Jahr.

groups.name: Places
groups.intro: Places are often neuter or feminine. Learn the article with the place, because you will need it after prepositions.

groups.name: Body
groups.intro: Body parts are mostly masculine or neuter; die Hand and die Nase are the common feminine ones.

groups.name: Clothing
groups.intro: Clothing is a mix of genders — a good set to drill because there is no reliable rule.

groups.name: Nature & weather
groups.intro: Weather words are common in small talk: das Wetter, der Regen, die Sonne.

groups.name: Work & school
groups.intro: Note the -in ending for female people: der Lehrer / die Lehrerin.

groups.name: Transport
groups.intro: Vehicles are a good test of gender: der Zug, die Bahn, das Auto, das Fahrrad.

groups.name: sein, haben, werden
groups.intro: The three most important verbs. Learn them by heart — they are irregular and appear everywhere. Format: 3rd person present, past, perfect.

groups.name: Everyday verbs
groups.intro: High-frequency regular and mixed verbs. Drop -en for the stem, then add the ending: ich -e, du -st, er -t.

groups.name: Modal verbs
groups.intro: Six verbs that rewrite the sentence around them. The modal goes in position 2 and the main verb moves to the end in the infinitive.

groups.name: Separable verbs
groups.intro: The prefix detaches and lands at the end of the sentence: Ich stehe um sieben auf.

groups.name: Common irregular verbs
groups.intro: Strong verbs change their stem vowel. Learn the principal parts (present, past, perfect) together with the meaning.

groups.name: Everyday adjectives
groups.intro: Common adjectives used to describe people and things.

groups.name: Personalpronomen (ich, du, er …)
groups.subtitle: Subject pronouns
groups.intro: Subject pronouns: ich, du, er/sie/es, wir, ihr, sie/Sie. du is one person (informal), ihr is several people (informal), Sie is polite for one or many.

groups.name: sein / haben (Präsens)
groups.subtitle: to be / to have
groups.intro: sein (to be): ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie/Sie sind. haben (to have): ich habe, du hast, er/sie/es hat, wir haben, ihr habt, sie/Sie haben. Both are irregular — learn them by heart.

groups.name: Artikel: der/die/das, ein/eine
groups.subtitle: Definite & indefinite articles
groups.intro: Definite: der (m), die (f), das (n). Indefinite: ein (m/n), eine (f). In the nominative the article only shows gender; the accusative will change masculine forms.

groups.name: Plural der Nomen
groups.subtitle: Plural nouns
groups.intro: German has five plural patterns: -e, -er, -en/-n, -s, and no ending (sometimes with an umlaut). The plural article is always die.

groups.name: Präsens regelmäßiger Verben
groups.subtitle: Regular verbs (present tense)
groups.intro: Drop -en from the infinitive to get the stem, then add: ich -e, du -st, er/sie/es -t, wir -en, ihr -t, sie/Sie -en.

groups.name: Präsens mit Vokalwechsel
groups.subtitle: Stem-changing verbs
groups.intro: Some common verbs change their vowel in the du and er/sie/es forms: e becomes i or ie, a becomes ä. ich, wir, ihr and sie/Sie stay regular.

groups.name: Nominativ & Akkusativ
groups.subtitle: Nominative & accusative
groups.intro: The subject is nominative, the direct object is accusative. Only masculine articles change: der → den, ein → einen, kein → keinen. die, das, eine and ein stay the same.

groups.name: Possessivartikel (mein, dein …)
groups.subtitle: Possessive articles
groups.intro: mein (my), dein (your), unser (our). The ending depends on the gender of the thing owned: mein Vater, meine Mutter, mein Kind.

groups.name: Wortstellung, Fragen, Negation
groups.subtitle: Word order, questions, negation
groups.intro: In a statement the conjugated verb is always in second position. In yes/no questions it comes first. Negate nouns with kein- (same endings as ein-); negate everything else with nicht.

groups.name: Modalverben (können, müssen …)
groups.subtitle: Modal verbs
groups.intro: können, müssen, wollen, sollen, dürfen, mögen. The modal is conjugated in position 2; the main verb goes to the end as an infinitive: Ich muss heute arbeiten.

groups.name: Trennbare Verben (auf-, ein-)
groups.subtitle: Separable verbs
groups.intro: Separable prefixes (auf-, ein-, an-, mit-, fern-) detach and go to the end of the clause: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.

groups.name: Imperativ (du, ihr, Sie)
groups.subtitle: Imperative
groups.intro: Three forms: du (stem, often no -e), ihr (normal present form without ihr), Sie (infinitive + Sie).

groups.name: Perfekt: haben/sein + Partizip II
groups.subtitle: The perfect tense
groups.intro: The spoken past: haben or sein + past participle. Movement and change-of-state verbs (gehen, fahren, kommen, aufstehen) use sein; most others use haben.

groups.name: Präpositionen der Zeit und des Ortes
groups.subtitle: Time & place prepositions
groups.intro: am + day/part of day, im + month/season/year, um + clock time, in + city/country. Learn these as fixed pairs.

groups.name: Zahlen, Datum und Uhrzeit
groups.subtitle: Numbers, dates and time
groups.intro: Clock time: um, halb (half to the next hour), Viertel nach / Viertel vor. Dates use ordinal numbers with am.

groups.intro: High-frequency verbs with principal parts.

groups.name: Work & office
groups.intro: Abstract work nouns: note that -ung, -schaft and -keit are feminine, while -ling and -or tend to be masculine.

groups.intro: Type the correct article for each noun.

groups.name: Plural forms

groups.name: Society & media
groups.intro: Words ending in -ion and -ität are always feminine: die Information, die Universität.

groups.name: Feelings & abstract nouns
groups.intro: Abstract nouns are worth drilling early because they appear constantly in A2 reading.

groups.name: Travel & city
groups.intro: Travel vocabulary for A2: booking, trips and directions.

groups.name: Health
groups.intro: Health vocabulary pairs well with modal verbs and the imperative.

groups.name: Reflexive verbs
groups.intro: The action falls back on the subject: Ich freue mich. The reflexive pronoun changes with the person (mich, dich, sich, uns, euch).

groups.name: Verbs with the dative
groups.intro: These verbs take a dative object, not an accusative one: Ich helfe dir. Mir gefällt das.

groups.name: More irregular verbs
groups.intro: More strong and inseparable verbs that are common at A2. Inseparable prefixes (be-, er-, ver-, ent-) never separate.

groups.name: Describing the world
groups.intro: Wider set of everyday adjectives.

groups.name: Dativ: dem / der / dem
groups.subtitle: The dative case
groups.intro: The dative marks the indirect object and follows certain verbs (helfen, danken, gehören, folgen, antworten) and prepositions (mit, bei, aus, nach, von). Masculine der becomes dem, feminine die becomes der, neuter das becomes dem; plural die becomes den.

groups.name: Personalpronomen im Dativ (mir, dir …)
groups.subtitle: Dative pronouns
groups.intro: Dative personal pronouns are mir, dir, ihm, ihr, uns, euch, ihnen. They are used with dative verbs like helfen, danken, geben, gefallen, gehören, zeigen.

groups.name: Wechselpräpositionen (in, an, auf …)
groups.subtitle: Two-way prepositions
groups.intro: Wechselpräpositionen (in, an, auf, über, unter, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen) take the accusative for direction (Wohin?) and the dative for location (Wo?).

groups.name: Adjektivendungen nach der/die/das
groups.subtitle: Adjective endings after der/die/das
groups.intro: After the definite article (der/die/das, den, dem), adjectives take the weak endings -e or -en. The ending is -e in the nominative singular and accusative neuter/feminine, and -en everywhere else.

groups.name: Adjektivendungen nach ein/kein/mein
groups.subtitle: Adjective endings after ein/kein/mein
groups.intro: After ein/eine/kein/mein the adjective takes the strong ending where the article has no ending (masc. nom. -er, fem. nom. -e, neut. nom./acc. -es, masc. acc. -en) and -en in the dative and plural.

groups.name: Präteritum
groups.subtitle: The simple past
groups.intro: The Präteritum is the simple past, common in writing. Learn the forms of sein (war), haben (hatte), and the modal and strong verbs: ging, kam, sah, konnte, musste.

groups.name: Nebensätze mit dass / weil / wenn
groups.subtitle: Subordinate clauses
groups.intro: After the conjunctions dass, weil, wenn (and ob), the conjugated verb moves to the end of the clause.

groups.name: Komparativ und Superlativ
groups.subtitle: Comparative & superlative
groups.intro: The comparative adds -er (schnell → schneller), the superlative uses am -sten or the + -ste. Learn the irregulars gern/lieber/am liebsten and gut/besser/am besten.

groups.name: Reflexive Verben (Akkusativ)
groups.subtitle: Reflexive verbs
groups.intro: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun that refers back to the subject: mich, dich, sich, uns, euch, sich. Common ones: sich freuen, sich interessieren, sich treffen, sich beeilen, sich waschen, sich erinnern.

groups.name: Konjunktiv II: hätte, wäre, würde
groups.subtitle: Konjunktiv II basics
groups.intro: Konjunktiv II expresses polite requests and unreal conditions. Common forms: hätte (haben), wäre (sein), würde + infinitive (for most other verbs).

groups.name: Relativsätze
groups.subtitle: Relative clauses
groups.intro: Relative clauses are introduced by a relative pronoun (der, die, das, den, dem …) that agrees with the noun it refers to. The conjugated verb goes to the end of the clause.

groups.name: Genitiv: des / der
groups.subtitle: The genitive case
groups.intro: The genitive shows possession. Masculine and neuter nouns take des + -s (des Mannes), feminine and plural take der (der Frau, der Kinder).

groups.intro: High-frequency adjectives with comparison forms.

groups.intro: High-frequency nouns with their article and plural.

groups.name: Character & quality
groups.intro: Adjectives for describing character, moods and quality.

groups.name: Infinitiv mit zu
groups.subtitle: Infinitive with zu
groups.intro: Use zu + infinitive after verbs like vergessen, versuchen, vorhaben and after expressions like Es ist wichtig. With separable verbs, zu goes between the prefix and the stem: aufstehen -> aufzustehen.

groups.name: um … zu / damit
groups.subtitle: Purpose clauses
groups.intro: Use um ... zu + infinitive when both clauses have the same subject. When the subjects are different, use damit + a full clause.

groups.name: Temporalsätze (als, wenn, nachdem …)
groups.subtitle: Time clauses
groups.intro: als is used for a single event in the past, wenn for repeated events or the future, nachdem for an earlier action, bevor for a later action, and während for something happening at the same time. The conjugated verb goes to the end of the clause.

groups.name: Indirekte Fragen (ob, W-Frage)
groups.subtitle: Indirect questions
groups.intro: In indirect questions the verb moves to the end. Use ob for yes/no questions and a question word (wann, wo, wie, was) when the question starts with one.

groups.name: Plusquamperfekt
groups.subtitle: The past perfect
groups.intro: The Plusquamperfekt describes the earlier of two past events. Use hatte or war (Präteritum of haben/sein) + the past participle. Use war with verbs that form the perfect with sein.

groups.name: Passiv: werden + Partizip II
groups.subtitle: The passive voice
groups.intro: The passive is formed with werden + past participle: Das Haus wird gebaut. In the past use wurde/wurden + past participle: Das Haus wurde gebaut.

groups.name: Futur I (werden + Infinitiv)
groups.subtitle: The future
groups.intro: Futur I is werden + infinitive: Ich werde dich anrufen. In everyday German the present tense is very often used for the future: Morgen gehe ich zum Arzt.

groups.name: Konjunktiv II (Vergangenheit, irreale Bedingung)
groups.subtitle: Konjunktiv II
groups.intro: Konjunktiv II expresses unreal situations and polite requests. Learn hätte, wäre, würde. For the past, use hätte/wäre + past participle: Ich hätte dir geholfen.

groups.name: Verben mit Präpositionen (warten auf …)
groups.subtitle: Verbs with prepositions
groups.intro: Many German verbs take a fixed preposition. Learn them together: warten auf (+ Akk.), sich freuen auf/über (+ Akk.), denken an (+ Akk.), sich interessieren für (+ Akk.), Angst haben vor (+ Dat.).

groups.name: Konnektoren und Wortstellung
groups.subtitle: Connectors and word order
groups.intro: deshalb (therefore), trotzdem (nevertheless) and außerdem (besides) are adverbs: they take position 1, so the verb comes next (inversion). denn (because) is a coordinating conjunction and keeps normal word order.

groups.name: Präpositionen mit Genitiv (wegen, trotz …)
groups.subtitle: Genitive prepositions
groups.intro: The prepositions wegen (because of), trotz (despite), während (during) and statt (instead of) take the genitive: wegen des Regens, trotz des Wetters, während der Pause, statt des Autos.

groups.name: N-Deklination (der Junge → den Jungen)
groups.subtitle: Weak masculine nouns
groups.intro: Some masculine nouns (der Junge, der Student, der Kollege, der Nachbar, der Kunde, der Mensch) add -en or -n in every case except the nominative singular: der Junge, den Jungen, dem Jungen, des Jungen.

groups.name: Useful B2 verbs
groups.intro: Common verbs for discussion and argument.

groups.name: B2 adjectives
groups.intro: Adjectives for nuanced description and argument.

groups.name: Konjunktiv II der Vergangenheit (hätte gemacht)
groups.subtitle: Konjunktiv II: past
groups.intro: Past unreal: hätte/wäre (Konjunktiv II of haben/sein) + past participle. Use hätte for most verbs and wäre for verbs of motion/change plus sein, bleiben and werden.

groups.name: Irreale Bedingung: wenn / Verb-erst
groups.subtitle: Unreal conditions
groups.intro: Unreal conditions use Konjunktiv II. A conditional can drop 'wenn': the verb then moves to the front (Hätte ich Zeit, …), and the main clause often starts with 'dann'.

groups.name: Konzessivsätze (obwohl, trotzdem …)
groups.subtitle: Concessive clauses
groups.intro: 'obwohl' and 'auch wenn' introduce a subordinate clause (verb goes last). 'trotzdem' and 'dennoch' are adverbs that begin the main clause, so the verb stays in second position.

groups.name: Irrealer Vergleich: als ob / als
groups.subtitle: Irreal comparison: als ob
groups.intro: For irreal comparisons use 'als ob' or 'als wenn' + Konjunktiv II (verb last after ob). With bare 'als' the verb comes second: Er tut, als wäre er krank.

groups.name: Zweiteilige Konnektoren (entweder … oder, je … desto)
groups.subtitle: Two-part connectors
groups.intro: Two-part connectors pair up: entweder … oder, sowohl … als auch, nicht nur … sondern auch, zwar … aber, je … desto (je + verb last, desto + comparative + verb second).

groups.name: Passiversatzformen (sein + zu, sich lassen)
groups.subtitle: Passive alternatives
groups.intro: The werden-passive can be replaced by: sein + zu + infinitive (= can/must be done), sich lassen + infinitive, or an active sentence with 'man'.

groups.name: Partizipien als Adjektive
groups.subtitle: Participles as adjectives
groups.intro: Partizip I (infinitive + d) is active/ongoing (das schlafende Kind); Partizip II is passive/completed (die gebaute Brücke). They take normal adjective endings.

groups.name: Nominalisierung (Verben → Nomen)
groups.subtitle: Nominalisation
groups.intro: Verbs and adjectives can become nouns. Infinitives become neuter nouns (das Lesen, das Schwimmen); adjectives take suffixes like -heit/-keit/-ung (die Freundlichkeit, die Lösung).

groups.name: Subjektive Modalverben (Vermutung)
groups.subtitle: Subjective modal verbs
groups.intro: Modal verbs express assumptions: müssen = very likely, dürfte = probably, könnte = possibly, soll = reportedly (what others say).

groups.name: Futur II (werden + Partizip II)
groups.subtitle: The future perfect
groups.intro: Futur II = werden + past participle + haben/sein. It describes an action completed in the future, or an assumption about the past (Er wird angekommen sein).

groups.name: Relativsätze mit was, wo, wer
groups.subtitle: Relative clauses: was, wo, wer
groups.intro: 'was' is used after alles, nichts, etwas or to refer to a whole clause; 'wo' replaces a place preposition; 'wer' introduces a free relative clause as the subject (Wer …, der …).

groups.name: Adjektive mit Präpositionen (interessiert an …)
groups.subtitle: Adjectives with prepositions
groups.intro: Many adjectives govern a fixed preposition: interessiert an, stolz auf, abhängig von, Angst vor, bekannt für, zufrieden mit, verantwortlich für, gespannt auf.

groups.name: Erweiterte Partizipialattribute (die von ihm geschriebene E-Mail)
groups.subtitle: Extended participle attributes
groups.intro: An extended participle attribute stands between the article and the noun: article + extra information + participle + adjective ending + noun (die von ihm geschriebene E-Mail). The participle takes the normal adjective ending.

groups.name: Partizipialkonstruktionen
groups.subtitle: Participial clauses
groups.intro: Participial clauses replace subordinate clauses and contain no finite verb. The participle leads the clause and its subject must match the subject of the main clause (Von der Reise erschöpft, ging sie ins Bett).

groups.name: Funktionsverbgefüge (zur Verfügung stehen)
groups.subtitle: Noun + verb phrases
groups.intro: Fixed noun+verb units where the noun carries the meaning and the verb is 'light' (zur Verfügung stehen = to be available). Learn each noun together with its fixed preposition and verb.

groups.name: Konjunktiv I (indirekte Rede)
groups.subtitle: Konjunktiv I
groups.intro: Konjunktiv I marks indirect speech, letting a speaker report without endorsing. Key forms: sein → sei, haben → habe, werden → werde; most other verbs add -e (er komme, er müsse).

groups.name: Nominalstil vs. Verbalstil
groups.subtitle: Nominal vs. verbal style
groups.intro: Nominal style replaces a verb or clause with a noun, typically formed with -ung or -heit/-keit, or with an infinitive used as a noun. It is characteristic of formal and academic German.

groups.name: Konnektoren (C1: sofern, zumal, indes)
groups.subtitle: Advanced connectors
groups.intro: Advanced connectors: sofern (provided that), zumal (especially since), insofern (insofar / as far as), indes (while / however), and freilich / allerdings (admittedly / however).

groups.name: Wortbildung (Präfixe, Suffixe)
groups.subtitle: Word formation
groups.intro: Prefixes and suffixes change meaning: un- = not, miss- = wrongly; -heit / -keit / -ung turn adjectives or verbs into nouns, and -bar means '-able'.

groups.name: Vorfeldbesetzung (Betonung)
groups.subtitle: Fronting for emphasis
groups.intro: Any element can take the Vorfeld (position 1) for emphasis or theme-rheme structure, but the finite verb then stays in position 2 (Gestern habe ich ... gearbeitet).

groups.name: Ausklammerung
groups.subtitle: Extraposition
groups.intro: Heavy or informationally important elements can be moved out of the sentence bracket and placed after the finite verb (Ich habe ihn gesehen, den Mann).

groups.name: wer / was auch immer, egal wie
groups.subtitle: Whatever / whoever
groups.intro: Indefinite relative clauses: wer = 'whoever', was = 'whatever'; was auch immer / egal wie = 'whatever / no matter how'.

groups.name: Präpositionale Attribute (das Interesse an …)
groups.subtitle: Prepositional attributes
groups.intro: Many nouns take a fixed preposition: Interesse an, Angst vor, Wunsch nach, Hoffnung auf, Freude über, Zweifel an, Kritik an, Mangel an.

groups.name: Register & Stilebenen (gehoben / umgangssprachlich)
groups.subtitle: Register & style
groups.intro: German distinguishes register: colloquial (kriegen, kaputt), neutral, formal/elevated (erhalten, defekt) and literary (Antlitz, verscheiden). Choose the word that matches the register.

groups.name: Distanz-Konjunktiv I (Presse)
groups.subtitle: Reportive Konjunktiv I
groups.intro: In press and reporting, Konjunktiv I signals that a claim is being quoted rather than endorsed (Er sagte, er sei ...; die Zahl sei gestiegen).

groups.name: Komplexe Nominalsyntax (Genitivketten)
groups.subtitle: Complex noun phrases
groups.intro: Long noun phrases stack genitives and nested attributes (die Entscheidung des Gerichts der zweiten Instanz). The article must agree with the noun it directly precedes.

groups.name: Idiomatik (Redewendungen)
groups.subtitle: Idioms
groups.intro: Fixed idiomatic expressions (Redewendungen) whose meaning is not literal: jemandem die Daumen drücken, den Nagel auf den Kopf treffen, ins Fettnäpfchen treten.

groups.name: Gehobene Kollokationen (Kritik üben)
groups.subtitle: Elevated collocations
groups.intro: Elevated verb+noun collocations: eine Entscheidung treffen, Kritik üben, Wert legen auf, eine Rede halten, Konsequenzen ziehen, eine Diagnose stellen.

groups.name: Seltene und literarische Formen
